title: Theorem
body_md: (Corollary~\ref{cor-Goren-inj-cot}) Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a Grothendieck category with a set of generators of finite projective dimension, and let $\mathcal{S}$ be any set of objects. Let $\mathcal{B} := \mathcal{S}^{\perp}$.  Then $({}^\perp \mathcal{GI}_{\mathcal{B}}, \mathcal{GI}_{\mathcal{B}})$ is a  perfect cotorsion pair. That is,  the class ${}^\perp \mathcal{GI}_{\mathcal{B}}$ is covering and the class $\mathcal{GI}_{\mathcal{B}}$ is enveloping.
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $\mathcal{K}$ be a category and $\lambda$ a regular cardinal.
By a $\lambda$-direct limit, denoted $\varinjlim M_i$,  we mean the colimit of a directed system $\{M_i, f_{ij}\}$ indexed by some $\lambda$-directed poset.   We say that $\mathcal{K}$ \emph{has $\lambda$-direct limits} if colimits of such diagrams always exist.
\begin{enumerate}
\item  An object $M\in\mathcal{K}$ is called \emph{$\lambda$-presentable} if $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal{K}}(M,-)$ preserves $\lambda$-direct limits.
\item We say that $\mathcal{K}$ is \emph{$\lambda$-accessible}  if it has $\lambda$-direct limits and possesses a set $T$ of $\lambda$-presentable objects such that every object of $\mathcal{K}$ is a $\lambda$-direct limit of objects from $T$. By an \emph{accessible} category we mean one that is $\lambda$-accessible for some regular $\lambda$.
\item We say that $\mathcal{K}$ is \emph{locally $\lambda$-presentable}  if it is cocomplete and $\lambda$-accessible. By a \emph{locally presentable} category we mean a cocomplete accessible category.
\end{enumerate}

label: def-accessibly-embedded
title: Definition
head: environment

label: lemma-acc-embed
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(1) $\impliedby$ (2).  Assume that the inclusion $\mathcal{B} \hookrightarrow \mathcal{K}$ is a $\lambda$-accessible functor.  Given any $\lambda$-directed system $\{B_i, f_{ij}\}$ of morphisms between objects of $\mathcal{B}$, we are asserting that any colimit for it in $\mathcal{K}$ is in fact in $\mathcal{B}$. But a colimit cone $(\varinjlim B_i, \{\eta_i\})$   does exist in $\mathcal{B}$, and by  hypothesis it also serves as a  colimit cone in $\mathcal{K}$. Any other colimit in $\mathcal{K}$ for $\{B_i, f_{ij}\}$ must be isomorphic to $\varinjlim B_i\in\mathcal{B}$. So the strictly full assumption implies that \emph{any}  colimit of  $\{B_i, f_{ij}\}$ in $\mathcal{K}$ must be in $\mathcal{B}$.


\noindent  (1) $\implies$ (2).  Assume $\mathcal{B}$ is closed under $\lambda$-direct limits in $\mathcal{K}$. We are to show that the inclusion preserves $\lambda$-direct limits. So again let $\{B_i, f_{ij}\}$  be a $\lambda$-directed system of morphisms between objects in $\mathcal{B}$.  Let $(\varinjlim B_i, \{\eta_i\})$ be a  colimit cone for it, but in $\mathcal{K}$.
By hypothesis,  $\varinjlim B_i \in \mathcal{B}$. Since the subcategory is full, each  $\eta_i \colon B_i \xrightarrow{} \varinjlim B_i$ is also in $\mathcal{B}$.  Likewise, for any  `imposter' cocone in $\mathcal{B}$,  the unique map $h \colon \varinjlim B_i \xrightarrow{} B$  in $\mathcal{K}$ satisfying the universal property must also be in $\mathcal{B}$, by the fullness. It follows that $(\varinjlim B_i, \{\eta_i\})$ is indeed the  colimit cone for the system $\{B_i, f_{ij}\}$, in $\mathcal{B}$, and that the inclusion preserves the colimit cone.

label: lemma-raising-acc-index
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Statement (1) follows from~\cite[Them.~2.11(i)/Def.~2.12]{adamek-rosicky} and ~\cite[Remarks~2.18(2)]{adamek-rosicky}.

We prove (2).  We first observe that if $B\in\mathcal{B}$ is  $\lambda$-presentable relative to  $\mathcal{K}$, then $B$ is also $\lambda$-presentable relative to the accessible category $\mathcal{B}$.   Indeed the former means that the functor $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal{K}}(B, -)  \colon \mathcal{K} \xrightarrow{} \textbf{Set}$ preserves $\lambda$-direct limits.
  Since the restriction of this functor to $\mathcal{B}$ is exactly $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal{B}}(B, -)  \colon \mathcal{B} \xrightarrow{} \textbf{Set}$, it follows from Lemma~\ref{lemma-acc-embed}(2) that $B$ is $\lambda$-presentable relative to $\mathcal{B}$.  So we have shown  $\lambda$-presentablility in $\mathcal{K}$ implies $\lambda$-presentability in  $\mathcal{B}$. So by combining  this with statement (1), we have that for any  regular cardinal  $\lambda' \vartriangleright \lambda$:  If $B\in\mathcal{B}$ is  $\lambda'$-presentable relative to  $\mathcal{K}$, then $B$ is also $\lambda'$-presentable relative to   $\mathcal{B}$.
  On the other hand, it  follows from~\cite[Uniformization Theorem~2.19]{adamek-rosicky} that there  exist  (arbitrarily large)  regular cardinals $\mu \vartriangleright \lambda$ such that, conversely,  the inclusion functor takes $\mu$-presentable objects of $\mathcal{B}$ to $\mu$-presentable objects of $\mathcal{K}$. (The proof constructs a particular regular $\lambda' \vartriangleright \lambda$ such that this is the case for  any other regular $\mu \vartriangleright \lambda'$.)

label: them-rightperp-accessible
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
This proof follows the one in~\cite[Prop.~4.7]{adamek-rosicky}, combined with  the existence of sets of generating monomorphisms as shown in~\cite{saorin-stovicek}. The latter result can also be found in~\cite[\S9.6]{gillespie-book}. Indeed by~\cite[Prop.~9.29]{gillespie-book} there exists a set  $I_{\mathcal{S}} =\{k : K \rightarrowtail X\}$ of generating monics for $\mathcal{B} := \mathcal{S}^{\perp}$. This means that $Y \in \mathcal{B}$ if and only if for any $k \colon K \rightarrowtail X$ in $I_{\mathcal{S}}$ and  any morphism  $f \colon K \xrightarrow{} Y$, there exists an extension of $f$ along $k$.  Now if we take any regular cardinal $\lambda$ such that the domain of each $k \in I_{\mathcal{S}}$ is $\lambda$-presentable, then $\mathcal{B} = \mathcal{S}^{\perp}$ is closed under $\lambda$-direct limits; see~\cite[Lemma~12.5]{gillespie-book}. In other words, the full subcategory $\mathcal{B} \subseteq \mathcal{K}$ is  $\lambda$-accessibly embedded in the sense of Definition~\ref{def-accessibly-embedded}.
Note that we are free to choose our regular $\lambda$ so that both the domain and the codomain of each $k \in I_{\mathcal{S}}$ is $\lambda$-presentable and also so that $\mathcal{K}$ is  $\lambda$-accessible. Then again $\mathcal{B} \subseteq \mathcal{K}$ is  $\lambda$-accessibly embedded and we now can easily argue that $\mathcal{B}$ is closed under $\lambda$-pure subobjects (and this is analogous to the proof  of~\cite[Lemma~3]{krause-approximations and adjoints}).  Indeed assume $p \colon P \rightarrowtail B$ is a $\lambda$-pure (in $\mathcal{K}$) subobject of some $B\in \mathcal{B}$. We wish to show $P \in \mathcal{B}$, and for this it is enough to show that   for any $k \colon K \rightarrowtail X$ in $I_{\mathcal{S}}$ and  any given morphism  $f \colon K \xrightarrow{} P$, there exists an extension of $f$ along $k$. But given such an $f$, since $B \in \mathcal{B}$, we do have that the composite $pf$ admits such an extension, call it $g$. Diagrammatically, the solid arrows provide a commutative square in $\mathcal{K}$
$$\begin{tikzcd}[ampersand replacement=\&]
K \arrow[r, rightarrowtail, "k"] \arrow[d, "f" '] \& X \arrow[dl,  , dashed, "\exists" ']  \arrow[d,  "g"] \\
P  \arrow[r, rightarrowtail, "p"] \& B.
\end{tikzcd}$$
By the very definition of $p$ being $\lambda$-pure, a dashed arrow $X \xrightarrow{} P$ exists so that the upper left triangle commutes. That is, $f$ extends over $k$, proving   $P \in \mathcal{B}$.
It  follows from the aforementioned~\cite[Cor.~2.36]{adamek-rosicky}  that $\mathcal{B} \subseteq \mathcal{K}$ is an accessibly embedded, accessible subcategory.
In particular, the proof there shows that there is  a regular $\lambda' \vartriangleright \lambda$  such that  $\mathcal{B}$ is $\lambda'$-accessible ($\lambda'$ is called $\mu$ in the proof there). Note then that $\mathcal{K}$ too is  $\lambda'$-accessible, and still, $\mathcal{B}\subseteq \mathcal{K}$ is $\lambda'$-accessibly embedded. It follows from Lemma~\ref{lemma-raising-acc-index}(2) that we can  raise the regular cardinal  $\lambda'$ to   arbitrarily  large ones  $\mu \vartriangleright \lambda'$ such that the statement in (2) holds. For such regular cardinals $\mu$, we have that $\mathcal{B}\subseteq \mathcal{K}$ is again a $\mu$-accessibly embedded, $\mu$-accessible subcategory and the proof is complete.

label: cor-injectives-accessible
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor-injectives-accessible}
For any Grothendieck category $\mathcal{G}$ there exists a regular cardinal $\mu$ such that  $\mu$-direct limits of injectives are again injective, and there is a set (not a proper class)  $T$ of $\mu$-presentable injective objects  such that every injective object is a $\mu$-direct limit of objects from $T$.

title: Definition
body_md: $A = \{A_j\} \subseteq \mathcal{G}$ be any set of objects. We let $\varinjlim A$ denote the \emph{direct limit closure} of $A$. By this we mean the class of all objects equal to the colimit of some directed system of objects from $A$.

title: Notation
body_md: Given any class of objects $\mathcal{B}\subseteq \mathcal{G}$, we let $\mathcal{I}_{\mathcal{B}}$ denote the class of all (not necessarily exact) $\mathcal{B}$-acyclic chain complexes of injectives.
head: environment

label: them-A-acyclic-model
title: Theorem
head: environment

label: eq-iso
title: Proof
body_md:
By Baer's criterion, the set of all $\{\,U_i/C\,\}$ where $C$ ranges through all subobjects of each $U_i$, cogenerates the categorical injective cotorsion pair, $(\mathcal{G},\mathcal{I})$,  in our ground category $\mathcal{G}$. We define a set of complexes $\mathcal{S}$ as follows where  all of the $n$'s  range through $\mathbb{Z}$:
\[
\mathcal{S} = \{D^{n} (U_i/C) \,|\, U_i \in\mathcal{U} , \ \forall C \subseteq U_i\} \bigcup   \{S^{n} (A_j) \,|\, A_j \in A \}.
\]
One checks that $\mathcal{S}^{\perp} = \mathcal{I}_A$.
Indeed by~\cite[Prop.~4.4]{gillespie-degreewise-model-strucs}, the right Ext-orthogonal to the set $$\{D^{n} (U_i/C) \,|\, U_i \in\mathcal{U} , \ \forall C \subseteq U_i\}$$ is precisely the class of all  complexes of injectives.  So then $\mathcal{S}^{\perp}$ is precisely the class of all complexes of injectives $X$ such that $$\operatorname{Ext}^{1}_{\textnormal{Ch}(\mathcal{G})}(S^{n}(A_j),X) = 0$$
 for  all $n$ and all $A_j\in A$.
 But since $X$ is a complex of injectives, one can show (see  \cite[Cor.~10.22 and Exer.~10.4.1]{gillespie-book}) that  for a $\mathcal{G}$-object $M$ we have an isomorphism
\begin{equation}\label{eq-iso}
  \tag{$\dagger$}
\operatorname{Ext}^{1}_{\textnormal{Ch}(\mathcal{G})}(S^{n}(M),X) \cong H_{n-1}[\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal{G}}(M,X)].
 \end{equation}
From this it follows that $\mathcal{S}^{\perp} = \mathcal{I}_A$.

Now defining $\mathcal{W} := {}^\perp \mathcal{I}_A$, we have  that $(\mathcal{W}, \mathcal{I}_A)$ is a cotorsion pair that is cogenerated by $\mathcal{S}$. We note that both $\mathcal{W}$ and $\mathcal{I}_A$ are closed under suspensions (shifts).  The isomorphism in~(\ref{eq-iso}) is a special case of the well-known isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Ext}^{1}_{dw}(\Sigma^{n}W,X) \cong H_{n-1}[\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal{G}}(W,X)],$$
between degreewise split extensions of complexes and the homology of the total hom complex.
(For example, see again  \cite[Cor.~10.22]{gillespie-book}.) The characterization of $\mathcal{W}$ stated in (3)  follows from this isomorphism. What we have asserted in (2) follows from the special case isomorphism shown above in~(\ref{eq-iso}).


It follows easily from property (3)  that $\mathcal{W}$ is closed under direct summands and satisfies the 2 out of 3 property on short exact sequences. It is also clear that $\mathcal{W}$ contains all contractible complexes. This includes  the categorically injective complexes, which are precisely the contractible complexes of injectives, as well as the generating set $\{D^n(U_i) \,|\, U_i\in\mathcal{U}\}$ for the Grothendieck category $\textnormal{Ch}(\mathcal{G})$. From these two facts it follows  that  $(\mathcal{W}, \mathcal{I}_A)$ is a (cofibrantly generated and functorially complete) injective cotorsion pair; see~\cite[Prop.~2.21(4) and Them.~9.34]{gillespie-book}. It is then automatic from~\cite[Prop.~3.2]{gillespie-ding-modules} that $\mathcal{W}$ is closed under direct limits. (This can also be found in~\cite[Cor.~9.57]{gillespie-book}.)

At this point we have constructed a cofibrantly generated abelian model structure $$\mathfrak{M} = (All, \mathcal{W}, \mathcal{I}_A)$$ on $\textnormal{Ch}(\mathcal{G})$ having all of the properties listed in (1), (2),  and (3). The   properties listed in (4) follow automatically from general statements; see~\cite[Them.~10.27 and~10.29 and Cor.~12.24]{gillespie-book}.

To finish, let us make  clear that  $\mathcal{I}_{\mathcal{B}} = \mathcal{I}_A$.
Because of the containments $$A \subseteq \mathcal{B} \subseteq \varinjlim A,$$ we clearly have that for any complex $X$  of injectives,
$$\textnormal{$X$ is  $(\varinjlim A)$-acyclic $\implies$ $X$ is  $\mathcal{B}$-acyclic $\implies$  $X$ is  $A$-acyclic.}$$
  But it follows immediately from the properties stated in (1) and (2)   that
  $$\textnormal{$X$ is $A$-acyclic $\implies$ $X$ is  $(\varinjlim A)$-acyclic.}$$  So the three types of acyclicity coincide. In particular, $\mathcal{I}_A = \mathcal{I}_{\mathcal{B}}$.

title: Remark
body_md:
Although we will not use it in this paper, it seems worth pointing out that Theorem~\ref{them-A-acyclic-model} is in fact a corollary of a more general theorem. The reader will note that  the notion of an $A$-acyclic complex $X$ of injectives (Definition~\ref{def-A-acyclic})  applies equally well to any set $A = \{A_j\}$ of \emph{chain complexes} over $\mathcal{G}$, not just $\mathcal{G}$-objects.  Indeed one just uses acyclicity of the total hom complex $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal{G}}(A_j,X)$ for complexes $A_j \in A$.  Then the analogous statement of Theorem~\ref{them-A-acyclic-model}, and its proof go through in the same way. One just adjusts the cogenerating set  in the proof to be the more general  set \[
\mathcal{S} = \{D^{n} (U_i/C) \,|\, U_i \in\mathcal{U} , \ \forall C \subseteq U_i\} \bigcup   \{\Sigma^{n}A_j \,|\, A_j \in A \}.
\]
The rest of the proof goes through in the same way.

title: Notation
body_md: Given any class of objects $\mathcal{B}\subseteq \mathcal{G}$, we let $\textnormal{\footnotesize{ex}}{\mathcal{I}}_{\mathcal{B}}$ denote the class of all \emph{exact} $\mathcal{B}$-acyclic chain complexes of injectives. (See Definition~\ref{def-A-acyclic}.)
head: environment

label: them-exact-B-acyclic-models
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{them-exact-B-acyclic-models}
Let $A = \{A_j\} \subseteq \mathcal{G}$ be any set of objects and let   $\mathcal{B}$ be any class of objects  such that $A \subseteq \mathcal{B} \subseteq \varinjlim A$. Assume $\mathcal{G}$ admits a set $\mathcal{U}$ of generators such that each $X \in  \textnormal{\footnotesize{ex}}{\mathcal{I}}_{\mathcal{B}}$ is $\mathcal{U}$-acyclic.  Set $\widehat{A} = A\cup\mathcal{U}$.
Then $\mathcal{I}_{\widehat{A}} = \textnormal{\footnotesize{ex}}{\mathcal{I}}_{\mathcal{B}}$ and applying Theorem~\ref{them-A-acyclic-model} to the set $\widehat{A}$ yields a cofibrantly generated abelian model structure
$$\mathfrak{M}_{\widehat{A}} = (All, \mathcal{W}, \textnormal{\footnotesize{ex}}{\mathcal{I}}_{\mathcal{B}})$$
with all of the properties (1)--(4) listed there.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Of course by taking the set $A$ to be $\widehat{A}$ in  Theorem~\ref{them-A-acyclic-model} we do get a model structure, $\mathfrak{M}_{\widehat{A}} = (All, \mathcal{W}, \mathcal{I}_{\widehat{A}})$, with all of the properties listed there. We only need to show that $\mathcal{I}_{\widehat{A}} =  \textnormal{\footnotesize{ex}}{\mathcal{I}}_{\mathcal{B}}$, the class of all exact $\mathcal{B}$-acyclic complexes of injectives.

\noindent $(\subseteq)$
Assume  $X \in \mathcal{I}_{\widehat{A}}$. Then, by definition, $X$ is a complex of injectives that is both $A$-acyclic and $\mathcal{U}$-acyclic. By Theorem~\ref{them-A-acyclic-model}, $\mathcal{I}_{\mathcal{B}} = \mathcal{I}_A$, so $X$ is $\mathcal{B}$-acyclic.  Being also $\mathcal{U}$-acyclic  implies that $X$ itself is exact, as $\mathcal{U}$ is a set of generators.

\noindent $(\supseteq)$ On the other hand, if $X\in\textnormal{\footnotesize{ex}}{\mathcal{I}}_{\mathcal{B}}$, then certainly it is $A$-acyclic, as $A\subseteq \mathcal{B}$. By hypothesis, $X$ is also $\mathcal{U}$-acyclic. This means $X$ is in $\mathcal{I}_{\widehat{A}}$. \\
 This shows  $\mathcal{I}_{\widehat{A}} =  \textnormal{\footnotesize{ex}}{\mathcal{I}}_{\mathcal{B}}$, and that is all that was needed to be shown.
head: environment

label: cor-exact-injectives-B-acyclic
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor-exact-injectives-B-acyclic}
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a  Grothendieck category and $(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{B})$ be a cotorsion pair that is cogenerated by a set.  Assume $\mathcal{G}$ admits a set $\mathcal{U}$ of generators such that each $X \in  \textnormal{\footnotesize{ex}}{\mathcal{I}}_{\mathcal{B}}$ is $\mathcal{U}$-acyclic.  Then there exists a set of objects $\widehat{T}$ for which $\mathcal{I}_{\widehat{T}} = \textnormal{\footnotesize{ex}}{\mathcal{I}}_{\mathcal{B}}$ and applying Theorem~\ref{them-A-acyclic-model} to the set $\widehat{T}$ yields a cofibrantly generated abelian model structure
$$\mathfrak{M}_{\widehat{T}} = (All, \mathcal{W}, \textnormal{\footnotesize{ex}}{\mathcal{I}}_{\mathcal{B}})$$
with all of the properties (1)--(4) listed there.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Precisely, let $T$ be a set as guaranteed by Corollary~\ref{cor-rightperp-accessible}.  Then as in Proposition~\ref{them-exact-B-acyclic-models}, set $\widehat{T} = T\cup\mathcal{U}$, and apply the theorem.

Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a Grothendieck category and let  $\textnormal{\footnotesize{to}}{\mathcal{I}}$ denote the class of all totally acyclic complexes of injectives.  Assume $\mathcal{G}$ admits a set $\mathcal{U}$ of generators such that each $X \in  \textnormal{\footnotesize{to}}{\mathcal{I}}_{\mathcal{B}}$ is $\mathcal{U}$-acyclic.

with all of the properties (1)--(4) listed there.

label: lemma-U-acyclicity
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma-U-acyclicity}
Assume that $\mathcal{G}$ is a  locally finite dimensional  Grothendieck category with $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i\}$  a set of generators of finite projective dimension.
Then a chain complex $X$ of injectives is exact (i.e. acyclic in the usual sense) if and only if it is $\mathcal{U}$-acyclic in the sense of Definition~\ref{def-A-acyclic}.
In particular,  each $X \in  \textnormal{\footnotesize{ex}}{\mathcal{I}}_{\mathcal{B}}$ is  automatically $\mathcal{U}$-acyclic for any class of objects $\mathcal{B}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: If $X$ is $\mathcal{U}$-acyclic then it is certainly exact, as $\mathcal{U}$ is a set of generators. (This holds for any set of generators.) For the converse we use that our generators are of finite projective dimension. Indeed if $X$ is an exact complex of injectives and $U_i \in \mathcal{U}$, then by dimension shifting we get $\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal{G}}(U_i, Z_nX) \cong \operatorname{Ext}^{1+j}_{\mathcal{G}}(U_i, Z_{n+j}X)$ and this vanishes for large enough $j$.  It follows that $X$ is  $\mathcal{U}$-acyclic.

label: def-G-inj-B-tate
title: Definition
head: environment

label: lemma-B-Tate-char
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma-B-Tate-char}
In Definition~\ref{def-G-inj-B-tate}, set $\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{G}} :=  \mathcal{W} \cap \mathcal{G}$. More formally, this is the class of objects in $\mathcal{G}$ defined by $$\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{G}} := \{\mkern2mu M  \in \mathcal{G}  \,|\, S^0(M) \in \mathcal{W} \mkern2mu \}.$$
Then we have  $\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{G}} = {}^\perp \mathcal{GI}_{\mathcal{B}}$, and this is exactly the class of all $\mathcal{B}$-Tate trivial objects.
Moreover, $\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{G}}$ is a thick class.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We have  $M\in {}^\perp \mathcal{GI}_{\mathcal{B}}$, if and only if,  $\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal{G}}(M, N) = 0$ for all $N \in \mathcal{GI}_{\mathcal{B}}$, if and only if,  $\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal{G}}(M, Z_0X) = 0$ for all $X \in \textnormal{\footnotesize{ex}}{\mathcal{I}}_{\mathcal{B}}$.
But there is a well-known isomorphism $$\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal{G}}(M, Z_0X) \cong \operatorname{Ext}^1_{\textnormal{Ch}(\mathcal{G})}(S^0(M), X)$$
which holds whenever $X$ is an exact chain complex.  (For example, the isomorphism is proved in~\cite[Lemma~4.2]{gillespie-degreewise-model-strucs}.) So the previous conditions happen if and only if $\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\textnormal{Ch}(\mathcal{G})}(S^0(M), X) = 0$ for all $X \in \textnormal{\footnotesize{ex}}{\mathcal{I}}_{\mathcal{B}}$, or, if and only if $S^0(M)\in {}^\perp \textnormal{\footnotesize{ex}}{\mathcal{I}}_{\mathcal{B}} =\mathcal{W}$. This is the case, by definition, if and only if, $M\in\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{G}}$.
This proves $\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{G}} = {}^\perp \mathcal{GI}_{\mathcal{B}}$.

Next, note that $M\in{}^\perp \mathcal{GI}_{\mathcal{B}}$ if and only if   $\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal{G}}(M, Z_nX) = 0$ for all $X \in  \textnormal{\footnotesize{ex}}{\mathcal{I}}_{\mathcal{B}}$, and all $n$.  Since $X$ is an exact complex of injectives it is easy to see that this is equivalent to saying  $M$ is  $\mathcal{B}$-Tate trivial in the sense of Definition~\ref{def-G-inj-B-tate}.

For $X\in \textnormal{\footnotesize{ex}}{\mathcal{I}}_{\mathcal{B}}$, we have $\operatorname{Ext}^{1}_{\textnormal{Ch}(\mathcal{G})}(\Sigma^{n}(-),X) \cong H_{n-1}[\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal{G}}(-,X)]$ (as in the proof of Theorem~\ref{them-A-acyclic-model}). It follows that $\mathcal{W}$ and hence $\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{G}} = \mathcal{W}\cap\mathcal{G}$  are both thick.

label: lemma-generators-cond

head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The equivalence of the  conditions on $\mathcal{U}$ follows immediately from Lemma~\ref{lemma-B-Tate-char}.
Next, assume  $({}^\perp \mathcal{GI}_{\mathcal{B}}, \mathcal{GI}_{\mathcal{B}})$ is a complete cotorsion pair.  Being Grothendieck, there does exist some set,  say  $\{G_i\}$, of generators for $\mathcal{G}$.  For each $i$, using  that $({}^\perp \mathcal{GI}_{\mathcal{B}}, \mathcal{GI}_{\mathcal{B}})$ has enough projectives, write  an epimorphism $W_i \twoheadrightarrow G_i$ with $W_i \in {}^\perp \mathcal{GI}_{\mathcal{B}}$. Then $\{W_i\}$ must also be a generating set for $\mathcal{G}$. In particular, ${}^\perp \mathcal{GI}_{\mathcal{B}}$ contains the generating set $\mathcal{U}:=\{W_i\}$.

The final statement was shown in Lemma~\ref{lemma-U-acyclicity}.

\label{lemma-W-perp}
$\mathcal{GI}_{\mathcal{B}} \subseteq \mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{G}}^{\perp}$.

title: Proof
body_md:
We have $\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{G}} = {}^\perp \mathcal{GI}_{\mathcal{B}}$ by Lemma~\ref{lemma-B-Tate-char}. So
$\mathcal{GI}_{\mathcal{B}} \subseteq ({}^\perp \mathcal{GI}_{\mathcal{B}})^{\perp} =  \mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{G}}^{\perp}$.

label: lemma-B-cot-pair
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma-B-cot-pair}
Let $\mathcal{V}$ be any thick class of $\mathcal{G}$-objects containing $\mathcal{B}$. If $(\mathcal{V}, \mathcal{V}^{\perp})$ is known to be a complete cotorsion pair, then this is an injective cotorsion pair with the property that $\mathcal{V}^{\perp}  \subseteq \mathcal{GI}_{\mathcal{B}}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Assume we have a complete cotorsion pair $(\mathcal{V}, \mathcal{V}^{\perp})$ where $\mathcal{V}$ is some thick class containing $\mathcal{B}$. We note that the cotorsion pair is necessarily hereditary; (this follows from the completeness and the thickness of $\mathcal{V}$. See~\cite[Lemma~2.3]{gillespie-recollement}.) Since $\mathcal{B}$ contains all of the injective objects, so does $\mathcal{V}$.
Then by a standard argument  we have that  $(\mathcal{V}, \mathcal{V}^{\perp})$ is in fact an injective cotorsion pair. That is,
$\mathcal{V}\cap\mathcal{V}^{\perp}$ is precisely the class of injective objects; see~\cite[Prop.~3.6(3)]{gillespie-recollement}. Now the argument given in~\cite[Them.~5.2]{gillespie-recollement} generalizes in a straightforward way to show that  each $N \in \mathcal{V}^{\perp}$ is equal to the 0-cycle of some exact $\mathcal{B}$-acyclic complex of injectives. The argument goes like this: Take a standard injective  coresolution of $N$. By the hereditary condition, each cokernel in the coresolution is again in $\mathcal{V}^{\perp}$.  To build the resolution the other way, start by taking a special $\mathcal{V}$-precover of $N$.  Then the precover must be an injective object and the kernel again is in $\mathcal{V}^{\perp}$. So we may iterate this process to get an injective \emph{resolution} of $N$, again with each kernel in $\mathcal{V}^{\perp}$. Pasting together the coresolution and the resolution we obtain an exact complex of injectives $X$, with $N = Z_0X$, and for which $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal{G}}(M,X)$ is exact whenever $M \in\mathcal{V}$. We are done since $\mathcal{B}\subseteq \mathcal{V}$.

title: Proof
body_md:
($\implies$) This is Lemma~\ref{lemma-generators-cond}.

\noindent ($\impliedby$)  Assume we have a set  $\mathcal{U}$ of $\mathcal{B}$-Tate trivial generators, or equivalently, that each $X \in  \textnormal{\footnotesize{ex}}{\mathcal{I}}_{\mathcal{B}}$ is $\mathcal{U}$-acyclic. Then  
we have the exact $\mathcal{B}$-acyclic  model structure of Corollary~\ref{cor-exact-injectives-B-acyclic},
$$\mathfrak{M}_{\widehat{T}} = (All, \mathcal{W}, \textnormal{\footnotesize{ex}}{\mathcal{I}}_{\mathcal{B}}).$$
Its construction shows  the cotorsion pair to be cogenerated by a set of chain complexes $\mathcal{S}$. (Explicitly, we have taken  $T$ to be a set as guaranteed by Corollary~\ref{cor-rightperp-accessible}  and then set $\widehat{T} := T\cup\mathcal{U}$. Then our explicit cogenerating set goes back to the proof of
Theorem~\ref{them-A-acyclic-model}, and in this case becomes
\[
\mathcal{S} = \{D^{n} (U_i/C) \,|\, U_i \in\mathcal{U} , \ \forall C \subseteq U_i\} \bigcup   \{S^{n} (A_j) \,|\, A_j \in \widehat{T} \}.)
\]
It follows from~\cite[Remark~1.8 and Prop.~2.9(1)]{stovicek-deconstructible} that there exists a set $\mathcal{S}' \supseteq \mathcal{S}$ such that $\textnormal{Filt}(\mathcal{S}') = \mathcal{W}$. Here, $\textnormal{Filt}(\mathcal{S}')$ denotes the class of all transfinite extensions of objects in $\mathcal{S}'$.
Now let $\mathcal{S}'_{\mathcal{G}} := \mathcal{S}'\cap\mathcal{G}$, or more formally
$$\mathcal{S}'_{\mathcal{G}} := \{\mkern2mu M \in \mathcal{G} \,|\, S^0(M) \in \mathcal{S}' \mkern2mu \}.$$
 Then
$\mathcal{S}'_{\mathcal{G}} \subseteq \mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{G}}$. If $M\in
\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{G}}$, then $S^{0}(M) \in \mathcal{W}$, and so the complex $S^0(M)$ must be
a transfinite extension of objects of $\mathcal{S}'$.  However, each complex
$X_{\alpha}$ in this transfinite extension is necessarily a subobject of
$S^{0}(M)$, and as such must again be of the form $S^{0}(M_{\alpha})$ for some object $M_{\alpha}$.
It follows that $M$ is a transfinite extension of objects in $\mathcal{S}'_{\mathcal{G}}$, and hence $\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{G}} = \textnormal{Filt}(\mathcal{S}'_{\mathcal{G}})$. So by ~\cite[Cor.~9.4]{gillespie-book} (Eklof's Lemma) we have $\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{G}} = \textnormal{Filt}(\mathcal{S}'_{\mathcal{G}}) \subseteq   {}^\perp (\mathcal{S'_{\mathcal{G}}}^{\perp})$. Since our generating set $\mathcal{U}$ is contained in $\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{G}}$, we have that
$({}^\perp (\mathcal{S'_{\mathcal{G}}}^{\perp}),  \mathcal{S'_{\mathcal{G}}}^{\perp})$ is a cofibrantly generated cotorsion pair; see~\cite[Def.~9.30 and Remark~9.31]{gillespie-book}. Since we already know that $\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{G}} = \textnormal{Filt}(\mathcal{S}'_{\mathcal{G}})$ is  closed under direct summands, we see from~\cite[Them.~9.34(2)]{gillespie-book} that $$({}^\perp (\mathcal{S'_{\mathcal{G}}}^{\perp}),  \mathcal{S'_{\mathcal{G}}}^{\perp}) =  (\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{G}}, \mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{G}}^{\perp})$$ and that this is a (functorially) complete  cotorsion pair.
 It now follows from Lemmas~\ref{lemma-W-perp} and~\ref{lemma-B-cot-pair} that  $\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{G}}^{\perp} = \mathcal{GI}_{\mathcal{B}}$ and that this is an injective cotorsion pair.

Finally, we comment on the enumerated properties. First, that $\mathcal{G}$ is well-generated follows from a general result (\cite[Cor.~12.24]{gillespie-book}) and the notion of a triangulated localization is discussed in~\cite[\S6.7]{gillespie-book}.
Property (2) follows from Lemma~\ref{lemma-B-cot-pair}. Finally, the Quillen equivalence stated in (3) will be proved in  Proposition~\ref{prop-quillen-equivalence}.

label: lem-cycles-of-W
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem-cycles-of-W}
 Let $\mathfrak{M}_{\widehat{T}} = (All, \mathcal{W}, \textnormal{\footnotesize{ex}}{\mathcal{I}}_{\mathcal{B}})$ be the exact $\mathcal{B}$-acyclic model structure of  Corollary~\ref{cor-exact-injectives-B-acyclic}.
Suppose $W$ is a complex with $H_{i}W=0$
for $i<0$ and $W_{i} \in \mathcal{B}$ for $i>0$.  Then $W \in\mathcal{W}$  if and only if $Z_0W \in \mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{G}}$. I.e., $S^0(Z_0W)\in \mathcal{W}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
This is the analog of~\cite[Lemma~5.1]{bravo-gillespie-hovey}, but we give an alternate proof.  
 By properties previously shown,  we have: (i) any disk $D^n(M)$ on any object $M\in\mathcal{G}$ is in the class $\mathcal{W}$, and (ii) any sphere $S^n(B)$, for any object $B \in \mathcal{B}$, is also in $\mathcal{W}$. From (i) we infer that any bounded above exact complex is trivial, as any such complex is a transfinite extension of disks. From (ii) we infer that any bounded below complex of objects from $\mathcal{B}$ is trivial, as any such complex is a transfinite extension of spheres $S^n(B_n)$ with each $B_n\in\mathcal{B}$.  Now the given chain complex $W$ has a subcomplex $Y \subseteq W$, where $Y$ is the bounded below complex $\cdots \xrightarrow{} W_2 \xrightarrow{} W_1 \xrightarrow{} Z_0W \xrightarrow{} 0$. Then note that $W/Y$ is (isomorphic to) the complex $0 \xrightarrow{} Z_{-1}W \xrightarrow{} W_{-1} \xrightarrow{} W_{-2} \xrightarrow{} \cdots$, which is bounded above and exact and so is trivial in the exact $\mathcal{B}$-acyclic model structure. Therefore, since the class of trivial complexes is thick, $W$ is trivial if and only if $Y$ is trivial. But we have another subcomplex, $S^0(Z_0W) \subseteq Y$, whose quotient is a bounded below complex of objects from $\mathcal{B}$. Thus $Y$ (and hence $W$) is trivial if and only if  $S^0(Z_0W)$ is trivial. That is,  if and only if $Z_0W \in \mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{G}}$.

label: prop-quillen-equivalence
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
That $(S^0, Z_0)$ is an adjoint pair is standard; see~\cite[Lemma~10.1(3)]{gillespie-book}. The left adjoint $S^0$ is clearly  exact and preserves trivial objects. It follows that $S^0$ preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations,  so $(S^0, Z_0)$ is indeed a Quillen adjunction~\cite[Prop.~7.7]{gillespie-book}.
To verify that this is a Quillen equivalence we will check the conditions in~\cite[Them~7.17(2)]{gillespie-book}. These conditions involve the unit and counit. We note that the unit  of the adjunction  $(S^0, Z_0)$  is merely the identity map $\eta_M \colon M \xrightarrow{} Z_0S^0(M)$. The counit is the evident inclusion $\epsilon_X \colon S^0(Z_0X) \xrightarrow{} X$.
 Now for an arbitrary (cofibrant) object $M\in\mathcal{G}$, we find a short exact sequence
\[
0 \xrightarrow{} S^{0}(M) \xrightarrow{} X \xrightarrow{}W \xrightarrow{} 0
\]
 with $X \in \textnormal{\footnotesize{ex}}{\mathcal{I}}_{\mathcal{B}}$ and $W\in\mathcal{W}$.  By applying the snake lemma (in degrees $0$ and $-1$) we get a short exact sequence
\[
0 \xrightarrow{} M \xrightarrow{} Z_{0}X\xrightarrow{} Z_{0}W \xrightarrow{} 0.
\]
It follows from Lemma~\ref{lem-cycles-of-W} that $Z_{0}W\in\mathcal{W}$, because the $W_{i} \in \mathcal{B}$ are injective for all $i\neq 0$ and $H_{i}W=0$ for all $i\neq 1$.  It follows that $M \rightarrowtail Z_0X$ is a trivial cofibration. This verifies the first condition (involving the morphism $j^{\#}$) in~\cite[Them~7.17(2)]{gillespie-book}. We now turn to the second condition (the one involving the morphism $p^{\flat}$). So let $X \in  \textnormal{\footnotesize{ex}}{\mathcal{I}}_{\mathcal{B}}$ be an arbitrary fibrant object. Since $Z_0X$ is already cofibrant, the map $p^{\flat}$ is just the evident inclusion  $\epsilon_X \colon S^0(Z_0X) \xrightarrow{} X$ that is the counit of the adjunction. We wish to show that it too is a weak equivalence (trivial cofibration) and for this it suffices to show that its cokernel is in $\mathcal{W}$. But this again follows from Lemma~\ref{lem-cycles-of-W}. Indeed  its cokernel is the complex
$$\cdots \xrightarrow{d_3}X_2  \xrightarrow{d_2}X_1  \xrightarrow{\pi d_1}X_0/Z_0X  \xrightarrow{\bar{d}_0}X_{-1}  \xrightarrow{d_{-1}}X_{-2} \xrightarrow{} \cdots $$
where $\bar{d}_0$ is the unique map satisfying $d_0 = \bar{d}_0\pi$. Since $X$ is an exact complex of injectives, this complex satisfies the hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem-cycles-of-W}, and so it is in $\mathcal{W}$ if and only if its 0-cycle is in $\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{G}}$ (trivial in the Gorenstein injective model structure on $\mathcal{G}$). But  the 0-cycle object of the above complex is clearly $\operatorname{Ker}{\bar{d}_0} = 0$, which is certainly in $\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{G}}$. This completes the proof that that $p^{\flat}$ is a trivial cofibration, and  that $(S^0, Z_0)$ is a Quillen equivalence.

The final statement follows from general  results; see~\cite[Thems.~7.12 and~7.17]{gillespie-book}.

label: cor-Goren-inj-cot
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor-Goren-inj-cot}
 The Gorenstein $\mathcal{B}$-injective cotorsion pair $(\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{G}}, \mathcal{GI}_{\mathcal{B}})$  of Theorem~\ref{them-Goren-inj-cot} is  perfect. That is,  the class $\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{G}}$ is covering and the class $\mathcal{GI}_{\mathcal{B}}$ is enveloping.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The class $\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{G}}$ is closed under direct limits. So the corollary follows from  a classical argument due to Enochs that can be found in \cite[\S2.2]{xu_flat_covers}. Although the arguments there are given for module categories, the results remain valid for Grothendieck categories (cf. \cite[\S2]{enochs2001}).
In particular, note that any special $\mathcal{GI}_{\mathcal{B}}$-preenvelope of an object $M$ is, in the terminology of \cite[Def.~2.2.1]{xu_flat_covers},  a \emph{generator for $\operatorname{Ext}(\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{G}}, M)$}. Then the existence of Gorenstein injective envelopes follows from~\cite[Prop.~2.2.1/Them.~2.2.2]{xu_flat_covers}. Likewise, the existence of $\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{G}}$-covers follows from~\cite[Them.~2.2.12]{xu_flat_covers}.
head: environment

title: Corollary
body_md: $\textnormal{St}(\mathcal{GI}_{\mathcal{B}})\subseteq \textnormal{St}(\mathcal{G})$ is a reflective subcategory. Indeed, Gorenstein injective approximations (i.e. special preenvelopes)  determine a functor $$R \colon\, \textnormal{St}(\mathcal{G}) \xrightarrow{}  \textnormal{St}(\mathcal{GI}_{\mathcal{B}})$$ which  is left adjoint to the inclusion functor $\textnormal{St}(\mathcal{GI}_{\mathcal{B}})\hookrightarrow \textnormal{St}(\mathcal{G})$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: This follows from~\cite[Prop.~3.10]{gillespie-book}. In particular,  take  $\lambda$ (see~\cite[Setup 3.2.2 on page~63]{gillespie-book} to be $\lambda = \omega := \mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{G}} \cap \mathcal{GI}_{\mathcal{B}}$, which is exactly the class of injective objects.

label: qco
title: Example
body_md:
\label{qco}
Let $\mathbb{X}$ be a quasi-compact and semi-separated scheme, with $\{U_i\}_{i=1}^N$ a semiseparating open affine covering of $\mathbb{X}$. We let $\textnormal{Qco}(\mathbb{X})$ denote the category of quasi-coherent sheaves on $\mathbb{X}$. Then $\textnormal{Qco}(\mathbb{X})$ admits a family of \emph{very flat} generators, as introduced by Positselski in \cite{positselski-contraherent-cosheaves}, and all such sheaves have finite projective dimension not exceeding $N$.
In more detail, by \cite[Cor.~4.1.2 (b), Cor.~4.1.4 and Lemma B.1.2]{positselski-contraherent-cosheaves}, the pair of classes $(\mathcal{VF}(\mathbb{X}), \mathcal{CA}(\mathbb{X}))$ of very flat and \emph{contraadjusted} quasi-coherent sheaves on $\mathbb{X}$ forms a complete hereditary cotorsion pair on $\textnormal{Qco}(\mathbb{X})$. In particular, $\mathcal{VF}(\mathbb{X})$ contains a set of generators for $\textnormal{Qco}(\mathbb{X})$. Now, by \cite[Lemma~5.5.12(c)]{positselski-contraherent-cosheaves}, together with the equivalent conditions (3) and (4) of \cite[Lemma B.1.9(c)]{positselski-contraherent-cosheaves}, it follows that every very flat quasi-coherent sheaf has finite projective dimension not exceeding $N$.

Therefore,  the Gorenstein injective model structure exists on $\textnormal{Qco}(\mathbb{X})$, and every quasi-coherent sheaf has a Gorenstein injective envelope. We note that the Quillen equivalence of Proposition~\ref{prop-quillen-equivalence} strengthens our previous result  from~\cite[Them.~5.2]{estrada-gillespie-quillen-duality}, which was for semi-separated Noetherian schemes.
head: environment

label: example-Krause
title: Example
body_md:
\label{example-Krause}
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a locally noetherian Grothendieck category whose derived category is compactly generated. In \cite[Them.~7.12]{krause-stable-derived}, Krause shows that  the objects with vanishing Tate cohomology, along  with the Gorenstein injectives,   form a complete cotorsion pair in $\mathcal{G}$. In particular, the compact generation implies the existence of Tate trivial generators for $\mathcal{G}$.
head: environment

label: example-FP_n
title: Example
body_md:
\label{example-FP_n}
For any Grothendieck category $\mathcal{G}$,  
 there is a set $\mathcal{S}$ of isomorphism representatives for all objects of type $\operatorname{FP}_n$ in the sense of~\cite{bravo-gillespie-perez-fpn}. (This fact is nicely explained in~\cite[\S2.2]{bravo-odabasi-parra-perez-fpn}.)
Such a set cogenerates the class $\mathcal{B} :=\mathcal{S}^{\perp}$, of all $\operatorname{FP}_n$-injective objects. So whenever $\mathcal{G}$ is locally finite dimensional we obtain Gorenstein $\operatorname{FP}_n$-injective envelopes and model structures. It is notable that we previously only knew this  in the  case that $\mathcal{G}$ is, in addition, an  \emph{$n$-coherent} category in the sense of~\cite{bravo-gillespie-perez-fpn}.  (For example,  Gorenstein injectives when $\mathcal{G}$  is locally noetherian,   Ding injectives when $\mathcal{G}$ is locally coherent, etc. See  \cite[Remark~6.3]{bravo-gillespie-perez-fpn}.)
head: environment

title: Example
body_md: Following \cite{li-guan-ouyang-strongly-fp-injective}, a module $N$ over a ring $R$ is said to be \emph{strongly FP-injective}  if $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(F,N) = 0$ for all finitely presented modules $F$ and all $i\geq 1$. A number of authors have studied these modules. For example, see~\cite{bazzoni-hrbek-positselski-fp-projective periodicity, emmanouil-kaperonis-k-absolutely-pure}. Let $\mathcal{SFI}$ denote the class of all strongly FP-injectives. Choose a set $\mathcal{S} = \{\Omega^n(F)\}$ of all syzygies of all the modules in some set of isomorphism representatives for the finitely presented modules. Then one can check that we have  $\mathcal{S}^{\perp} = \mathcal{SFI}$.  Thus we obtain Gorenstein $\mathcal{SFI}$-injective envelopes and model structures for any ring $R$.

label: ex-P-tate
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex-P-tate}
If $\mathcal{G}$ admits a set $\mathcal{U}$ of $\mathcal{P}$-Tate trivial generators, then taking $A = \mathcal{U} = \mathcal{B}$ in Theorem~\ref{them-A-acyclic-model} immediately yields $\mathfrak{M}_{\mathcal{U}} = (All, \mathcal{W}, \textnormal{\footnotesize{ex}}{\mathcal{I}})$. This is the injective model structure for Krause's stable derived category of $\mathcal{G}$. The related recollement also holds in the same way as~\cite[Cor.~5.8]{gillespie-models-for-hocats-of-injectives}.
